verdict.rationale: The IRS documents a dedicated test environment for its MeF machine channel, the Assurance Testing System (ATS). It has per-form test scenarios, known-issues tables, ATS-specific guidelines (Pub 1436), test packages (Pub 5078) and separate ATS vs Production certificates, and developers are told to validate in ATS before Production. It is not public, though: access requires e-file provider enrollment and e-Services sign-in, it opens only in dated seasonal windows, and the schemas and WSDLs are registration-gated. missing for 10: publicly accessible sandbox without enrollment or credentialing, year-round availability, publicly downloadable interface definitions for testing, independent or hands-on corroboration of end-to-end testing.

support.subject: As a developer, a public sandbox or test environment for the service's machine channel is documented — I can exercise the rail end to end before touching production

citations.quote: The IRS documents a dedicated test environment for its Modernized e-File system: the Assurance Testing System (ATS)

Transmitters, software developers, and state agencies are encouraged to review their implementations and complete any necessary changes in ATS prior to the Production deployment to avoid service disruptions.
